title: Acyclic-resolution comparison for underlying abelian sheaves of prime modules
statement: Let $i:Y\to X$ be a scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $r$ prime. Suppose the restriction on global sections is an isomorphism for every $\mathbf F_r$-module-valued etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Suppose that for every injective such sheaf $J$, the underlying abelian sheaf of $i^{-1}J$ has zero cohomology in all positive degrees [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then for every module-valued sheaf $M$ on $X$ and every $q\geq0$, the canonical pullback on abelian cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf $U(M)$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $H^q(X,U(M))\to H^q(Y,i^{-1}U(M))$, is bijective [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].

proof.text: In degree zero apply the strengthened comparison theorem, proved using the canonical degree-zero pullback formula.

Induct on q, simultaneously for all module sheaves M. The injective effacement ladder gives J,Q and right exact rows in degrees q and q+1. The induction hypothesis makes the first two vertical maps bijective. Naturality of cohomologyMap gives the first commuting square and the ladder gives the second. Apply Mathlib AddMonoidHom.bijective_of_surjective_of_bijective_of_right_exact to conclude bijectivity for M in degree q+1.

proof_origin.place: Dimension-shifting induction from right exact ladders; no full resolution comparison needed
